what: OD2 tier 2 "observed elsewhere": Hongqiao (ZSSS) movements identified from open ADS-B outside the Shanghai coverage gap. Aggregate counts only; per-flight data stays in refs/cache (local).

inputs.pair_check: Wikipedia SHA rev 1385154959, PVG rev 1385155113 destination lists (CC BY-SA 4.0)

days.sigma_note: 1-sigma uncertainties (1.4826 x median |out-of-sample error|), not error bounds: for normal errors about 32 % of movements are further off than their 1-sigma

gap_split.rule: cut a SHA/PVG-route flight at a coverage gap longer than the air time of its longest DB leg (M1 line) + 30 min, at most 4 h

inverse.rule: coverage ends (begins) airborne within 60-450 km of ZSSS, track within 15 deg of the bearing to (from) ZSSS, no landing (take-off) seen

validation.sign: errors are predicted - actual for M2 (negative = SHA event predicted too early for arrivals), actual - predicted air time for M1
validation.note_used: *_used: the estimate actually used: bias removed (nested, out of sample) only in bins where that cut sigma by >= 5 %; *_hkg_tpe_corrected: the held-out route with those same corrections

readings.identified_share: 69-70 % of 783.4/day carry a real identity and a DB-consistent track; that is an upper figure. The SHA-vs-PVG label was checked externally only on the Hong Kong and Taipei Songshan routes (C2: HKIA 51/51 and TSA 12/12 DB labels, 23/23 listed B1 movements); domestic labels rest on the DB. About 65-70 % is the defensible share.
readings.sigma: sigma is a 1-sigma uncertainty from out-of-sample validation, not an error bound
readings.registry_independence: not independent: the readsb identity fields come from tar1090-db, which is built from the Mictronics database plus the ADS-B Exchange basic aircraft DB, so the 100 % agreement with Mictronics is circular (consistency, not truth)

attribution: Contains information from ADSB.lol (https://adsb.lol), made available under the ODbL; routes: Virtual Radar Server standing data (CC0 1.0); aircraft data: Mictronics aircraft database (ODC-By 1.0)
